{{Top}}
'''Blue Six''' was the [[Callsign/Legends|call sign]] of the sixth member of Blue Squadron. There were a number of [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Squadron/Legends|squadrons]] with this name, and multiple [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] went by the call sign Blue Six.

==History==
[[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Ace Azzameen/Legends|Ace Azzameen]] flew as Blue Six for a [[Raid on the Suprosa|raid on the freighter ''Suprosa'']] as a member of a [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|Y-wing]] [[Blue Squadron (Bothan)|squadron]].<ref name="XWA">''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance]]''</ref><ref name="SOTE">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref>

A pilot designated "Blue Six" under the command of [[General/Legends|General]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] flew against [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] during a [[battle in the Milagro system]].<ref name="DFJK">''[[Dark Forces: Jedi Knight]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
According to the [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars'' Episode IV: ''A New Hope'' novel]], Blue Six was [[John D. Branon/Legends|John D. Branon]]. John D. ended up being [[Red Four/Legends|Red Four]] in the film. According to the [[Star Wars (1977)|''Marvel Star Wars'']] comic adaptation, Blue Six was [[Jek Tono Porkins/Legends|Jek Tono Porkins]]. Porkins eventually became [[Red Six/Legends|Red Six]] in the film.<ref name="ANHn">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars'' Episode IV: ''A New Hope'' novel]]</ref><ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref><ref name="MSW6">[[Star Wars (1977) 6|''Star Wars'' (1977) 6]]</ref>
